summary: X-band multimode pulse-Doppler fire-control radar, mechanically scanned (Gripen C/D)

system_loss_db.note: radome, ohmic, processing, straddle and CFAR losses together (assumed)

notch_ms.note: the main-beam clutter notch, half its width in radial speed (assumed)

angle_floor_beamwidths.note: the floor of each look's angle errors, a fraction of the plane's half-power beamwidth (SIM-M01, docs/sdk/radar-measurement-floors.md): assumed - no PS-05/A accuracy is published; the value is the documented default of a generic radar model's lower bound (mw-fusionradarsensor), the mechanisms behind such a floor (calibration, glint, multipath) those ll-est-track lists; the band 0.01-0.19 covers a precision fire-control radar's to a coarse one's
angle_floor_beamwidths.evidence: This value sets a lower bound on the azimuthal accuracy of the radar

range_floor_resolutions.note: the floor of each look's range errors, a fraction of its range resolution (SIM-M01): assumed, as angle_floor_beamwidths - the same model's documented default
range_floor_resolutions.evidence: This property sets a lower bound on the range accuracy of the radar

range_rate_floor_resolutions.note: the floor of each look's range-rate errors, a fraction of its Doppler resolution (SIM-M01): assumed, as angle_floor_beamwidths - the same model's documented default
range_rate_floor_resolutions.evidence: This property sets a lower bound on the range rate accuracy of the radar

medium_prfs.note: medium PRF: a dwell at 8 PRFs to resolve range and velocity (assumed, as for every one)

medium_m_of_n.note: a detection on 3 of the 8 (assumed, as for every one)

high_m_of_n.note: a detection on any of them (assumed)

false_alarm_time_s.note: the mean time between false alarms its threshold is set for: Stimson's for radars in fighter aircraft, "a minute or so", read as 60 s (the uncertainty covers the reading)
false_alarm_time_s.evidence: a false-alarm time of a minute or so is generally considered acceptable

average_power_w.note: its energy output (1 kW; over 10 kW at its peak)

class_calibration_db.note: its class (tube): minus the mean of the class's residuals against their published ranges, every radar of it alike, whoever made it: an-apg-68v9 +6.4, thomson-csf-rdi -5.6, n019 +5.4, n001 +11.1, ps-05a +0.3

stimson.title: G. W. Stimson, "Introduction to Airborne Radar", 2nd ed. (ISBN 1-891121-01-4), p. 144
stimson.verified: the sentence searched in the book itself (Google Books full-text search of this edition, 2026-10-07): "In radars for fighter aircraft, a false-alarm time" and "false-alarm time of a minute or so is generally considered acceptable" both match on p. 144, a control phrase ("an hour or so") does not; the page itself is not previewed

ll-est-track.title: Tracking and Parameter Estimation (Introduction to Radar Systems, slides EST&TRACK-1 to 41, 7/31/2008): slides 27-31
ll-est-track.verified: retrieved 2026-10-17, SHA-256 8ab4c3dd0a74f28a9efc1cbddd616d28b63f136293f70150781678791521bae9; its text read: slide 27 about 10:1 beam splitting at a ~13 dB threshold, slide 28 a bias error's definition, slides 30-31 the real-world limits (calibration, amplitude fluctuations, angle noise or glint, multipath) - mechanisms, no value for any radar

mw-fusionradarsensor.title: fusionRadarSensor (AzimuthBiasFraction, ElevationBiasFraction, RangeBiasFraction, RangeRateBiasFraction)
mw-fusionradarsensor.publisher: MathWorks, Sensor Fusion and Tracking Toolbox documentation, release R2026b
mw-fusionradarsensor.verified: read 2026-10-17: each bias fraction a fraction of that axis's resolution (the azimuth resolution typically the half-power beamwidth) that sets a lower bound on its accuracy; defaults 0.1 (azimuth, elevation) and 0.05 (range, range rate); no formula given. A proprietary generic model's documented convention, not data about this radar

validation.evidence: capable of detecting a fighter aircraft from 120 km distance
validation.note: the fighter of 4 m^2 its MK3 figures name: not fitted - its published power, aperture and band, the rest assumed
